misconceptions.description: Assuming Codex-generated code is good because it runs, without checking that the structure serves the learning interaction and authoring needs
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts generated code on the basis that it executes without error
misconceptions.feedback: Evaluate whether the structure supports the designed interaction and is maintainable, not only whether it runs. Working is not the same as well-designed.

misconceptions.description: Letting Codex choose the instructional content or interaction rather than implementing the designer's decisions
misconceptions.trigger: prompt asks Codex to decide what makes a good quiz or to pick questions
misconceptions.feedback: Specify the interaction, constraints, and content yourself. Use Codex to implement decisions you already made, not to make them.

misconceptions.description: Adopting a Codex feature suggestion as if it were a requirement instead of a proposal to judge against learning goals
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps a generated feature such as constant animation without weighing its effect on learning
misconceptions.feedback: Treat each suggestion as a proposal. Accept it only where it supports the learning goal; reject or scope it where it adds extraneous load or misleads.
